Remembering

Reviewed XORYA implementation, stack, restore behavior, and tier preferences

Worked for 33s

Surya, use Design 6 - Color-Coded Tier System as the final direction for XORYA Watchlist.

The goal: keep your existing watchlist functionality, but make the entire page feel like a premium streaming dashboard. Use cinematic background artwork, distinct colors for each tier, subtle glassmorphism, glowing borders, and a completely redesigned Google Drive restore section.

Below is the full implementation specification you can give to Antigravity, including color values, background-image treatment, component structure, interactions, responsive behavior, and implementation steps.

XORYA Watchlist - Final Design Specification

**Design direction: Color-Coded Tier System**

<text color="secondary" size="sm">Dark cinematic • Glassmorphism • Neon accents • Atmospheric artwork</text>
  Each watchlist tier gets its own identity, while the entire interface shares one consistent design system.
</box>

1. Overall page layout

Color behavior

Purple: collection and total-title indicators.

Green: completed titles and successful sync states.

Amber: currently watching.

Red: pending titles and the active Watching tier in the reference.

Blue/cyan: cloud connectivity and restore actions.

Important: colors must indicate state, not just decoration. Keep the same meaning in statistic cards, tier borders, icons and status indicators.

3. Background images - how to reproduce the cinematic look

The image you selected uses cinematic artwork behind the interface, not simply flat colored rectangles.

**Page atmosphere**

<text color="secondary" size="sm">Use subtle, low-opacity cinematic artwork behind the main page.</text>
  **Tier atmosphere**

<text color="secondary" size="sm">Use different ambient artwork or gradients in each tier panel.</text>

Where to get the images

Use existing TMDB assets first. Your XORYA site already uses TMDB metadata and artwork. Reuse the project's existing backdrop URLs where appropriate.

For the page background, create a collage from available backdrops or use one subtle, wide cinematic backdrop.

For individual tiers, use relevant posters/backdrops already associated with their contents, or create abstract CSS gradients for empty tiers.

For a custom decorative background, use a generated abstract cinematic texture. Keep it decorative and separate from real movie metadata.

Don't hardcode random movie titles or external image URLs into the tier components. Reuse existing image data and fallbacks.

CSS treatment

If using a real background image, layer it underneath the gradients with a dark overlay. Do not let the image reduce text contrast.

4. The redesigned Google Drive restore section

This section needs a major redesign. Replace the old “Cleared browser cache or history?” banner with a dedicated Sync & Restore Your Watchlist panel.

Sync & Restore Your Watchlist
      Keep your collection safe across devices.
    Connected
  Automatic backup
      Sync watchlist and episode progress.
  Cross-device access
      Continue across supported devices.
  Sync settings
    Restore from Drive →

Illustrative component preview. Connected status should only appear when the existing sync implementation confirms it.

Required behavior

Show a Google Drive icon, heading, short description, sync status and restore button.

Use a dark translucent surface with a thin cyan/blue border and subtle ambient glow.

Display accurate status labels such as Connected, Not connected, Syncing, Success or Failed.

Clicking Restore must call the existing restore workflow.

Provide loading, success, error and confirmation states.

Never imply that data is backed up when it is only stored locally.

Keep the existing Google authentication and restore logic intact.

5. Statistic cards

Build one reusable statistic card component, then supply different colors through configuration.

{#each [{name:"Total Titles",color:"#8B5CF6",icon:"layers"},{name:"Watched",color:"#10B981",icon:"check-circle"},{name:"Watching",color:"#F59E0B",icon:"eye"},{name:"To Watch",color:"#F43F5E",icon:"clock"}] as item}
    {item.name}
        Large numeric count, tinted background, matching border and subtle glow.
      {item.color}
  {/each}

Each card should include:

Large numeric count.

Icon at the top.

Label below the count.

Low-opacity artwork or a soft radial gradient.

Thin colored border and matching bottom progress line.

Subtle hover lift, without excessive animation.

Use actual counts from the current watchlist data. Do not hardcode zero.

6. Tier panels

Each tier is a separate content container with a colored header and border.

The tier header should contain:

Colored status dot.

Tier name.

Live item count.

Rename/edit action.

Sort and view controls, where already supported.

Add button.

Collapse/expand control.

Empty state should use a simple cinematic clapperboard illustration, subtle grid texture and short text. Do not show distracting poster collages when the tier has no items.

When populated, show the existing title cards inside the tier, with poster art, title, rating and existing actions. Preserve current add, remove, reorder and tier-management behavior.

7. Glassmorphism and component styling

Use consistent design tokens for all surfaces.

Example shared surface:

Apply this to cards, toolbars and restore panels. Keep backgrounds opaque enough for readability, and avoid adding strong glow to every single element.

8. Typography, spacing and interaction

Use the existing font if it already matches XORYA's branding; otherwise use a clean modern sans-serif.

Page heading: approximately 36-48px on desktop.

Card counts: approximately 30-36px.

Card labels: 13-15px.

Supporting text: 13-15px.

Main content padding: 24-40px on desktop.

Card gaps: 12-20px.

Panel padding: 18-24px.

Border radius: 12-22px, depending on component size.

Interactions:

Hover: slight lift, brighter border and gentle shadow.

Focus: visible keyboard focus ring.

Buttons: clear hover, active, disabled and loading states.

Transitions: approximately 180-250ms.

Respect prefers-reduced-motion.

On mobile, stack statistic cards into two columns and allow toolbar controls to wrap.

9. Implementation plan for Antigravity

**Audit existing code.** Find the watchlist page, tier component, statistic cards, Google Drive sync/restore flow, existing styles, and watchlist data model.
  **Create design tokens.** Add the color palette, shared glass-panel styling, spacing and border-radius variables.
  **Redesign the page shell.** Add cinematic atmosphere, improve heading hierarchy and align the main content.
  **Rebuild statistic cards.** Use one reusable component with four configurable color variants.
  **Redesign toolbar.** Improve New Tier, search, Cloud Sync, Export, Import and Reset without changing their behavior.
  **Replace the restore banner.** Build the new Sync & Restore panel and connect it to the existing Drive workflow.
  **Redesign tier containers.** Apply color-coded borders, headers, controls, empty states and populated layouts.
  **Polish and test.** Verify responsive layouts, data persistence, restore behavior, tier operations, loading states and accessibility.

10. Full Antigravity implementation prompt

# XORYA WATCHLIST - DESIGN 6 FINAL IMPLEMENTATION

Objective

Redesign the existing XORYA Watchlist page using the Color-Coded Tier System reference. The result must look like a premium, dark cinematic streaming dashboard with subtle glassmorphism, controlled neon accents, atmospheric backgrounds and clearly differentiated watchlist categories.

This is a redesign of the existing application, not a new application.

1. Preserve existing functionality

Before changing code, inspect the existing project and identify the actual watchlist components, data model, tier operations, Google Drive integration, authentication, local persistence, export/import and reset functionality.

Reuse existing functions, state, API calls and data structures. Do not invent replacement APIs or duplicate existing implementations.

Do not remove, break or silently change any working feature.

2. Design tokens

Use this palette:

Page background: #080B14

Primary surface: #101522

Raised surface: #151A29

Primary text: #F8FAFC

Secondary text: #9CA3B8

Purple / Total Titles: #8B5CF6

Green / Watched: #10B981

Amber / Watching: #F59E0B

Rose / To Watch: #F43F5E

Cyan / Cloud Sync: #38BDF8

Blue restore action: #2563EB

Create shared CSS variables and reusable components. Keep colors consistent across statistic cards, icons, tier borders, status indicators and focus states.

3. Page background

Use a deep navy-black background with subtle cinematic atmosphere.

Reuse suitable artwork already available through the project's TMDB integration where appropriate. Layer it with dark gradients and restrained color glows. Use CSS gradients when real artwork is unnecessary.

Never let background imagery reduce readability. Avoid large, bright images behind text.

4. Page header

Keep XORYA branding and existing navigation. Improve alignment, spacing, typography and visual consistency.

Add a clear Watchlist eyebrow, a prominent "Your Watchlist" heading and the subtitle "Organize by your mood, genre or priority."

Preserve all existing navigation routes and actions.

5. Statistic cards

Build one reusable statistic card component with configurable icon, label, value and accent color.

Display:

Total Titles - purple

Watched - green

Watching - amber

To Watch - rose

Use real values from existing watchlist state. Include large counts, clear labels, subtle background tint, matching border, a small accent line and restrained glow.

Ensure counts update immediately after relevant actions.

6. Toolbar

Redesign New Tier, Search, Cloud Sync, Export, Import and Reset into a clean, responsive toolbar.

Use consistent heights, rounded corners, subtle borders and clear active/disabled/loading states.

Keep every existing action operational. Preserve search behavior and existing confirmations for destructive actions.

7. Google Drive Sync & Restore panel

Replace the old "Cleared browser cache or history?" banner with a premium panel titled:

"Sync & Restore Your Watchlist"

Include:

Cloud or Google Drive icon

Short description of backup and restoration

Accurate connection/sync status

Restore from Google Drive action

Optional supporting indicators for automatic sync and cross-device access, but only when these features genuinely exist

Use a dark translucent surface, subtle blue/cyan glow, thin border and strong text hierarchy. Do not use a large generic green banner.

Connect the restore button to the existing restore workflow. Preserve Google authentication, backup format, conflict handling and data validation.

Display honest loading, success, failure and disconnected states. Never claim data is backed up when it is only stored locally.

8. Tier panels

Create or refactor a reusable tier container.

Each tier needs:

Colored status dot

Tier title

Live item count

Existing rename/edit actions

Existing sort/view controls

Add button

Collapse/expand action

Existing movie/series cards

Use rose for Watching, emerald for Completed, purple for To Watch, and existing user-selected colors for custom tiers where supported.

Use subtle tinted backgrounds, thin accent borders and controlled glow. Avoid making every component equally bright.

Preserve all tier creation, renaming, reordering, collapsing, deleting and title-management behavior.

9. Empty and populated states

For empty tiers, show a restrained clapperboard icon, subtle grid texture, "This tier is empty" and a short instruction to add movies or series.

For populated tiers, retain existing poster images, title metadata, ratings and working card actions.

Reuse existing title data and artwork. Never replace real content with hardcoded sample data.

10. Artwork strategy

Prefer existing TMDB backdrop/poster assets already used by the application. Reuse appropriate image data for cinematic decoration, with dark overlays and fallbacks.

Use CSS gradients for empty tiers. If a generated abstract background is needed, store it as a project asset and use it only decoratively.

Do not hardcode arbitrary external image URLs or create unnecessary image requests for each tier.

11. Glassmorphism and motion

Use consistent translucent surfaces, backdrop blur, subtle borders, soft shadows and restrained accent glows.

Apply small hover lifts and border-brightening transitions. Keep animation around 180-250ms and respect reduced-motion preferences.

Maintain readable contrast and visible keyboard focus indicators.

12. Responsive behavior

Desktop: four statistic cards in one row, a well-aligned toolbar and full-width tier panels.

Tablet: reduce spacing and allow toolbar controls to wrap.

Mobile: use two statistic columns, stacked sync content, compact tier headers and full-width controls where necessary. Prevent horizontal overflow.

13. Implementation sequence

Phase 1: Audit existing architecture and identify all relevant files and functionality.

Phase 2: Create design tokens and shared styles.

Phase 3: Redesign page background, heading and statistic cards.

Phase 4: Redesign toolbar.

Phase 5: Replace Google Drive restore banner and connect existing behavior.

Phase 6: Redesign tier headers, containers and empty/populated states.

Phase 7: Polish responsive behavior, interactions, contrast and accessibility.

Phase 8: Run available checks and test existing functionality.

Complete and verify each phase before proceeding. Avoid unrelated refactors.

14. Acceptance criteria

The result follows Design 6 rather than introducing a different visual direction.

All statistic counts are dynamic and accurate.

Every existing watchlist action still works.

Google Drive restore uses the existing integration.

Connection and backup status remain truthful.

Existing titles, tiers and episode progress remain intact.

Desktop, tablet and mobile layouts work without overflow.

No broken images, placeholder functionality or console errors introduced by the redesign.

Final response summarizes changed files, completed phases and tests performed.

Inspect the real project before coding. Adapt component names and implementation to the existing architecture rather than assuming particular file paths.

Recommended execution: give Antigravity the visual reference and this specification together. Have it complete and verify each phase before moving on, rather than attempting a full rewrite in one step.
